description: Farmers are price takers running a capital-intensive, weather-exposed, highly technical business on generational timescales. Ask about risk, debt, and decisions, not about the romance of the land.

questions.text: What decision do you make each year that you will not know the result of for months?
questions.lands_because: Captures the extraordinary feedback delay of agricultural decisions, which is what makes the judgment so hard and so different from most professions.
followups: What do you look at when you make that call?

questions.text: You do not set your price. What does that do to how you run the operation?
questions.lands_because: Stating the price-taker reality up front proves you understand the economics, and it opens directly into hedging, contracts, and cost control.
followups: How much of your risk management is marketing versus growing?

questions.text: What technology on your operation would surprise people who think farming has not changed?
questions.lands_because: Guidance systems, variable-rate application, moisture sensing, and genetics are all standard and all invisible to the public. Guests enjoy correcting the record.
followups: What has it actually changed about your yields or your hours?

questions.text: What year nearly ended it, and what got you through?
questions.lands_because: Nearly every multi-generation operation has one, and it carries drought, debt, markets, and family in a single story.
followups: Who did not make it through that year?

questions.text: How do you make a decision whose payoff lands after you are gone?
questions.lands_because: Soil, orchards, herd genetics, and succession all operate on generational time. This is a genuinely distinctive form of judgment worth a whole segment.
followups: Is there a next generation? Do you want there to be?

questions.text: What do people who write about food get wrong about how it is grown?
questions.lands_because: Invites correction of the food-media narrative from someone with standing to do it, without you having to take a side on any of it.
followups: Is there a criticism of your industry you think is fair?
